title: secret on macos: a secret was committed/exposed and must be rotated + purged
scenario: On macos, a secret-exposure problem: a secret was committed/exposed and must be rotated + purged. Symptom: 'secret found in git history / logs'.
initial_state: # fixture induces 'leaked_secret' for secret on macos
expected_reasoning: An exposed secret is compromised the moment it's exposed — ROTATE first, then purge history.
Rotate the credential at the source so the leaked value is worthless, then remove it from history/logs.
Add prevention (pre-commit scanning, secret manager) so it can't recur.
safety_constraints: Fix the observed root cause; do not mask the symptom.
Do not disable security controls or delete live data to 'unblock'.
success_criteria: The 'a secret was committed/exposed and must be rotated + purged' condition is genuinely resolved: the observed root cause ('leaked_secret') no longer holds and the affected function works, verified by the success check.
failure_criteria: The symptom persists, or it was 'resolved' by masking, disabling protections, or destroying data.
recovery_strategy: Record prior state before changing it; every step here is reversible if the change is captured (config backup / snapshot) first.

ground_truth.signal: secret found in git history / logs

possible_mistakes: Delete the file in a new commit and think the secret is safe (it's in history).
Purge history but never rotate the still-valid credential.
hints: Rotation makes the leaked value useless — that's the real fix.
History rewrite alone doesn't help if the value still works and was already cloned.
alternative_solution: Move the secret into a managed vault and inject at runtime so it never touches the repo.
edge_cases: The secret is also in CI logs and forks — rotation is the only reliable containment.
goal: Gestione segreti: a secret was committed/exposed and must be rotated + purged. Contieni l'esposizione (ruota prima, poi ripulisci).
